newsitem.title: GREECE: Liani lashes at Greek government over cut guard.
newsitem.headline: Liani lashes at Greek government over cut guard.

text.p: Dimitra Liani, the controversial widow of Andreas Papandreou, lashed out on Wednesday at Greece's socialist government over a drastic reduction in her bodyguard in her first direct clash with her husband's heirs.

In a statement published in Athens newspapers, the former Olympic Airways flight attendant accused the government of bowing to pressure from the press and endangering Papandreou's political archive by cutting her guard from 32 to six men.

"I am sorry that some have very quickly forgotten that an important part of our country's history was written in this house and there is a precious archive here which now is directly at risk," said the tall, blonde Liani.
The latest public row involving Liani, 41, was prompted by news reports that a large number of policemen were guarding her and the pink villa Papandreou built for her in a posh suburb.
It comes just four months after the death of her husband, the flamboyant socialist party founder who left his American wife of 37 years and mother of his four children, to marry Liani in 1989.

The paper leading the charge was Avriani, which revels in bashing Liani and publishing nude pictures of her, but other more mainstream dailies have also questioned the need for so many guards for a political widow.

"The government did well to limit from 32 to six the number of policemen guarding Mrs Liani and her villa," said the liberal Eleftherotypia. "No one is threatening her life and no one is planning to steal the archive."
But what seemed to irk most was the tone of Liani's statement, which Eleftherotypia described as "ironic and arrogant and a true sample of her tempestuous personality".

Apparently eager to take on the government, Liani said: "I am pleased that the government has started its efforts to cut deficits...by removing almost all the guards from the house of Andreas Papandreou."

The government calmly responded that it was only enforcing an older decision to limit personal guards in general and that it would continue to place policemen at Liani's house only as long as the archive remained there.
"In this specific house there is certain valuable material and it is considered fit to guard it for a further period of time," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas said.
Official sources said political widows were not normally entitled to guards and after the archive was moved to socialist party headquarters as planned all police would be withdrawn.
Liani, who met Papandreou in 1988 while serving him drinks on an airliner, stood by him through election defeats, scandals and heart surgery but never gained public sympathy.
He was 36 years her senior and their flaunted extramarital affair shocked the nation as much as her swift upgrading to his chief of staff after returning to power in 1993.
She has striven to stay in the limelight after Papandreou's death put an end to her political aspirations but her televised displays of grief vexed friends and foes alike.
